requests.text: Next step: replace the `{}` accumulator in `uniqueBy` with a `Map` and use `seen.has(k)` / `seen.set(k,true)`. This directly addresses E3 `typed-key-distinction` and `prototype-key-distinction` on `unique.mjs` version `12e22056d8ea59bbd956668f5b9f3587ff504d7568dc151b381ec04f56613c5d`: object keys stringify and consult the prototype chain, while `Map` preserves numeric-vs-string key identity and treats `"toString"`/`"__proto__"` as ordinary keys. Minimal full-fixture check after the edit: expect both `{id:1}` and `{id:'1'}`, both `{id:'toString'}` and `{id:'__proto__'}`, and both `{code:2}` and `{code:'2'}` to survive.

For E3 on `unique.mjs@12e22056...`, the failing checks `typed-key-distinction`, `prototype-key-distinction`, and `custom-key` point to plain-object key coercion/prototype lookup as the likely cause. A falsifiable next step is to back the `seen` set with a `Map` keyed by the raw `item[key]`, using `has`/`set`, then rerun those three checks on the new hash; the minimal distinguishing observation is that `1`/`'1'`, `toString`/`__proto__`, and `2`/`'2'` pairs are no longer dropped.

Next step: treat E3 (`typed-key-distinction`, `prototype-key-distinction`, `custom-key` on SHA `12e2205…`) as one unresolved key-identity/prototype-boundary issue, not a smoke-test gap. Falsifiable alternative: replace the plain-object `seen` lookup with an exact-value keyed store (e.g., Map/Set) and re-run those same three checks; minimal distinguishing observation: on that SHA, `[{id:1},{id:'1'}]` and `[{code:2},{code:'2'}]` must each retain both, while `[{id:'toString'},{id:'__proto__'}]` must retain both without inherited-name loss. If any still drops a value, that explanation is false; passing `empty-input`, `first-value-kept`, `original-order`, and `immutable-input` is not evidence for E3.

Concrete missing point for E3 on `unique.mjs@12e22056d8ea59bbd956668f5b9f3587ff504d7568dc151b381ec04f56613c5d`: swapping `{}` for `Object.create(null)` is not sufficient; it removes inherited prototype-name lookup, but property access still string-coerces keys, so `typed-key-distinction` (`1` vs `'1'`) and `custom-key` (`2` vs `'2'`) can still fail while `prototype-key-distinction` passes. If backing the accumulator with `Map`, key it by the raw `item[key]` and use `seen.has(k)` / `seen.set(k, ...)`, not truthiness. Re-run those three E3 checks; both members of each tested pair must remain.

Next step: replace the `{}` accumulator in `uniqueBy` with a `Map` keyed by the raw `item[key]`, using `seen.has(k)` / `seen.set(k,true)`; do not rely on `Object.create(null)` alone, because it removes inherited-name lookup but still string-coerces `1` vs `'1'`. Re-run the three E3 failures (`typed-key-distinction`, `prototype-key-distinction`, `custom-key`) on `unique.mjs@12e22056d8ea59bbd956668f5b9f3587ff504d7568dc151b381ec04f56613c5d`. Minimal distinguishing observation: both members of each tested pair remain — `{id:1}`/`{id:'1'}`, `{id:'toString'}`/`{id:'__proto__'}`, and `{code:2}`/`{code:'2'}`. If any pair still drops one, that explanation is false; the passing `empty-input`, `first-value-kept`, `original-order`, and `immutable-input` checks are not evidence for E3.
